title: Electronics II
full_title: Electronics II: Feedback, Op-Amps, Filters, and Data Converters
summary: Building on single transistors and simple stages, this course designs complete analog systems: feedback amplifiers and their stability, the internal design of operational amplifiers, output stages, active filters, oscillators, data converters and the noise that limits them all.
overview: Advanced analog is the one that the feedback and the op, amp and the filter and the converter is for, of the design, and the one that the limit is for. From feedback and the stability, through the output and the filter, to the oscillator and the converter and the noise, and the one that the design is for.

The feedback and the stability. The op, amp and the output stage. The filter and the oscillator. The converter and the noise. This course is the one that the design, and the one that the limit is for.
outcomes: Use the feedback and the stability, together, for a design.
Use the op, amp and the output stage, together, for a system.
Use the filter and the oscillator, together, for a signal.
Use the converter and the noise, together, for a design.

chapters.title: Feedback
chapters.summary: Negative feedback, loop gain, the four feedback topologies and their effect on gain, bandwidth and impedances.

chapters.title: Stability and frequency compensation
chapters.summary: Poles of feedback amplifiers, gain and phase margins, and dominant-pole and Miller compensation.

chapters.title: Operational amplifier design
chapters.summary: Two-stage CMOS and bipolar op-amps, specifications, slew rate, offset and common-mode range.

chapters.title: Output stages and power amplifiers
chapters.summary: Class A, B and AB output stages, efficiency, distortion and thermal considerations.

chapters.title: Active filter design
chapters.summary: Butterworth and Chebyshev approximations, Sallen–Key and biquad realisations, and switched-capacitor filters.

chapters.title: Oscillators
chapters.summary: The Barkhausen criterion, RC, LC and crystal oscillators, amplitude stabilisation and relaxation oscillators.

chapters.title: Data converters
chapters.summary: Sample-and-hold circuits, quantisation, DAC architectures, and flash, successive-approximation and sigma–delta ADCs.

chapters.title: Noise in electronic circuits
chapters.summary: Thermal, shot and flicker noise, noise models of devices and amplifiers, noise figure and low-noise design.
